title: Jaws
synopsis: A beach town, a Fourth of July, a chief who hates water, and a great white shark with a long memory.

nodes.text: Somebody has brought a guitar down to the bonfire and nobody can play it. The girl runs at the dune peeling off her clothes, laughing, and the boy who follows gets as far as the tideline before the beer takes his legs. She swims out past the bell buoy in easy strokes. Then she stops. She goes down, comes up, goes sideways, and the water takes her like a drain.

choices.consequence: You follow the beam out past the buoy until it stops moving, then starts moving the wrong way. You will describe that motion at three separate hearings.

You keep your back to the surf and your hands to the fire, and in the morning you tell the deputy you heard nothing over the singing. You choose to wait at the fire. By Mayor's Office, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Vaughn catches you between the ferry rail and the pharmacy with two selectmen and the town lawyer, all of them smiling at once. Amity is a summer town, he says. It needs summer dollars. He says it three different ways. Your beach-closing signs are stacked in the trunk of the cruiser, hand-lettered, still tacky, and he asks pleasantly whether you have looked at the ferry timetable lately.

choices.consequence: You say the word closed out loud with witnesses present. Vaughn's smile stays exactly where it is while his eyes go somewhere else entirely.

You settle for extra patrol boats and no signage. Three men in a Whaler is not a fence; it is a gesture you can be photographed making. You choose to compromise. By Coroner's Report, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The first report says shark. You read it twice, standing up, in a corridor that smells of floor wax. By four o'clock the coroner has a second opinion and the mayor's hand on his shoulder, and the word is propeller: a girl who swam into a passing boat, in the dark, alone, a mile out. There is correction fluid over one line of the typing.

choices.consequence: You photocopy the original before it can go missing and keep it folded in your tackle box. Nobody asks for it until August. You choose to document the original. By Boy on a Raft, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

You initial the amended sheet because the pen is already in your hand. Her mother will ask you, later, when exactly you knew. You choose to sign the edit. By Boy on a Raft, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: A yellow raft, a black dog barking at the surf, a woman calling a name toward the water in a voice that begins casual. The raft stands on end. Red spreads underneath it and closes over again. Two hundred people get to their feet on the sand at the same moment, and the sound they make is not screaming yet. It is the half second before screaming.

choices.consequence: You reach Mrs Kintner before anyone else and hold her arms while she fights you, and she screams into your uniform instead of the water. You help her. The way toward Town Hall opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

You do the job first, whistle and both arms up and everybody out, and by the time you turn around somebody else has hold of her. You commit to clear the beach. It carries you into Town Hall while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Folding chairs, bad coffee, a bounty already up to three thousand dollars from a woman who has never touched salt water. Then a fingernail goes down the chalkboard and every jaw in the room locks. Quint does not stand up to speak. He will take the fish for ten, he says, the head and the tail and the whole thing, and he prices it like a roofing job.

choices.consequence: You copy his number onto the back of the agenda while the room laughs him off the floor. It stays in your wallet for six weeks. You listen. The way toward Hooper Arrives opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

You let the chairman gavel him down. Quint collects his hat without hurry, because he already knows what week you will telephone. You brush him off. The way toward Hooper Arrives opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: He comes off the ferry with two crates of equipment, glasses he pushes up every thirty seconds, and money, which the dock notices first. He talks fast: bite radius, feeding pattern, an animal that does nothing but swim and eat and make more of itself. Then he turns over the amended coroner's report, reads two lines of it, and starts laughing at you in front of the harbourmaster.

choices.consequence: You hand him everything, including the page you were not supposed to keep, and he treats it as evidence rather than island gossip. You trust him. The way toward Tiger Shark Tied to the Dock opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

You keep him at arm's length for a day, and he spends the day on the dock measuring bite marks nobody else will look at. You commit to hesitate. It carries you into Tiger Shark Tied to the Dock while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Two amateurs bring in a tiger shark on a hand line and the whole town photographs itself beside it, Vaughn front and centre with his jacket buttoned. Hooper says the mouth is wrong: bite width, wrong build, wrong animal. The mayor says the crowd does not care about bite width, and he is correct. The tail drips onto the planking all afternoon while people queue to stand near it.
nodes.sceneTitle: Tiger Shark Tied to the Dock

choices.consequence: You and Hooper open the belly at midnight by torchlight and find a licence plate, a flattened tin can, and no part of any child. You choose to cut it open. By Night Dive, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

You let it hang for the newspapers. Whatever took the boy spends that night somewhere off the point with its stomach still full. You choose to skip the autopsy. By Night Dive, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Ben Gardner's boat rides at anchor with nobody aboard and a hole below the waterline you could walk through. Hooper goes down alone. Cold, silt, one column of torchlight. He works a tooth out of the splintered hull, big as his palm, white as a dinner plate, and then Gardner's face rolls slowly out of the gap at him, and his hand jerks open.

choices.consequence: He comes up far too fast, gasping, with nothing in his fist. Forty feet of silt keeps the only object that would have convinced anybody. You surface fast. The way toward Fourth of July opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

He gropes blind in the dark for ninety seconds and surfaces holding it. Vaughn turns it over once and asks who else has seen this. You commit to hold the tooth. It carries you into Fourth of July while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Vaughn walks a family into the shallows himself to make a point, hand flat on the man's back, smiling toward a reporter. Then a fin, then screaming, then two boys hauled out laughing under a cardboard dorsal. Everybody exhales. Everybody goes back in. And behind the sandbar, in the pond where the small children paddle and the rowboats go, something comes through the channel.

choices.consequence: You blow the whistle for the second time in ten minutes and half the beach ignores you, because you already cried wolf once today. You clear the water. The way toward Estuary opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

You leave it to the patrol boats. The pond is inside the channel, and nobody in the history of this town has watched the pond. You trust the patrol. The way toward Estuary opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Your older boy is in the pond in a borrowed sailboat with four friends and a life vest he is sitting on. A man in a rowboat goes over sideways without a sound. The dinghy comes apart in pieces. A leg sinks past the sandbar in water clear enough to read a newspaper through, while a hundred people scream from a beach forty yards off.

choices.consequence: You go in with your shoes on and drag Michael up the ramp yourself, and he does not say a word again until the hospital. You choose to pull him in. By Quint's Boat, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

You shout his name across open water as though that has ever worked. Somebody else's arms get him out. You arrive second, dry. You choose to yell. By Quint's Boat, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The Orca smells of diesel and fish blood and forty years of one man's habits. Jaws nailed over the wheelhouse door, harpoons racked, a compressor that only starts when kicked in the right place. Quint watches you carry your bag down the finger pier and observes, without any cruelty in it, that he has met your sort before: a chief of police who will not go in past his knees.

choices.consequence: You step across the gap in one motion and do not look at the water underneath. Quint notices that you did not look, and says nothing. You step on. The way toward Chum Line opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

You stand on the planks long enough that Hooper puts a hand out to help you, which is worse than falling in would have been. You commit to hesitate. It carries you into Chum Line while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The work is ladling ground fish over the transom for six hours while the boat crawls a grid, and the work is yours because it is the only thing aboard you are qualified to do. The slick spreads a mile behind you. Quint will not permit you to hold the ladle wrong. Your back goes. Your hands stink. Nothing comes. Nothing comes. Nothing comes.

choices.consequence: You fill the silence with island gossip until Quint tells you to stop chumming with your mouth, and Hooper laughs into his coffee. You commit to talk. It carries you into First Sight while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

You work the bucket for two hours without speaking, and Quint decides you may be tolerable, which he indicates by handing you a beer. You commit to stay quiet. It carries you into First Sight while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You are mid-sentence, complaining about the smell, when the water opens behind you. Snout first, then the gape, then teeth in staggered ranks going back into a hole you could stand upright in. It takes its time. It looks at you the way a man looks at a menu. It is gone again before you have finished backing into the cabin door.

choices.consequence: Quint puts the first barrel in behind the dorsal and the line sings off the rail, and the boat begins, very slowly, to be towed. You commit to tag the barrel. It carries you into Scars while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

You empty the rifle into a hole in the water. Quint takes the gun out of your hands and racks it again, almost gently. You commit to reach for the M1. It carries you into Scars while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Below decks, warm, working through Quint's bottle. He rolls a sleeve back for a moray eel off Cuba; Hooper counters with a bull shark and a thresher's tail. Arms on the table, laughing, everyone showing everything. Then Quint puts his ankle up: a burn scar where a tattoo used to be, a ship's name, taken off with a soldering iron. The laughing stops on his side of the table first.

choices.consequence: You lift your shirt over an appendix scar from when you were nine, and both of them are decent enough not to remark on the difference. You commit to show yours. It carries you into Indianapolis Speech while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

You keep your shirt down and offer a bar fight in Queens instead. It is a good story. It happened to somebody you knew. You commit to tell yours. It carries you into Indianapolis Speech while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: He tells it flat, hands still, eyes on the bottle. They delivered the bomb, took two torpedoes, and went down in twelve minutes with no distress signal sent. Hundreds of men floating in kapok jackets in warm water. The sharks arrived with the sun and worked the edges of the group, and every hour the group got quieter. He says the hard part was waiting your turn. He never wore a life jacket again.

choices.consequence: You do not move and you do not fill the pause, and Quint keeps going a long way past the point where he meant to stop. You choose to listen. By Shark Tested, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

You top up his glass because your hands want a job, and the story loses its thread somewhere near the rescue and never picks it up. You commit to pour another. It carries you into Shark Tested while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Three barrels in it now: yellow, floating, and then not floating. The line comes taut off the stern cleat, the transom dips, and the Orca starts travelling backward through her own wake. Water comes over the rail and across the deck and into your shoes. Quint's face, for the first time in your acquaintance with it, is doing arithmetic instead of theatre.

choices.consequence: You get a knife to the rope and Quint puts his boot on your wrist and leaves it there. The stern comes back up on its own, eventually. You cut the line. The way toward Engine Trouble opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

You lock both arms around the fighting chair and ride it out, and the fish takes three sealed barrels down with it and keeps them down. You hold on. The way toward Engine Trouble opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Quint runs the throttle past the last number on the dial and chases the thing down himself, laughing, spray coming over the bow in sheets. Something in the engine changes pitch: a knock, then a whine, then the smell of hot iron coming up through the cabin floor. Hooper is shouting about the ports. Quint has stopped listening to anybody aboard, including the boat.

choices.consequence: You reach past him and haul the throttle back yourself, and he does not hit you, which surprises both of you about equally. You commit to slow down. It carries you into Cage while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

You let him run it. The engine seizes at dusk with the radio already smashed on the deck and the shore a grey line behind you. You choose to push harder. By Cage, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The cage comes out of its crate looking like a shopping trolley somebody has welded. Hooper suits up with a lance and a hypodermic of strychnine and explains, twice, that he only has to get near the mouth. Quint measures the bar spacing with his eye and says nothing at all. Nobody mentions the obvious thing, which is that the animal is wider than the cage is tall.

choices.consequence: You work the winch and watch a friend go down into green water in a box you could bend open with a car jack. You commit to lower him. It carries you into Stern Crashing while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

You stall ten minutes checking a shackle that is perfectly fine. The delay costs you nothing except the last useful light of the day. You wait. The way toward Stern Crashing opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: It comes at the transom instead of the cage, and it comes over it. Wood goes. The stern drops, the deck tilts past anything you can stand on, and everything loose on it goes downhill: chairs, tanks, tackle boxes, the whole afternoon. Quint's fingers open on the varnish. He slides, unhurried at first, boots leading, still holding the machete and still not shouting.

choices.consequence: You get a hand around his ankle and hold on until the sound he is making changes, and then his boot is empty in your fist. You grab Quint's leg. The way toward Compressed Air Tank opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

You keep both hands on the rail and watch. That decision will sit in your chest at every town meeting for the next twenty years. You choose to hold the rail. By Compressed Air Tank, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The Orca is going down by the stern and there is a yellow scuba tank rolling loose in the water at the foot of the sloping deck. Hooper's lecture comes back word for word: do not drop them, do not knock them about, they go off like ordnance. You have a rifle with four rounds in it and a boat with perhaps six minutes left.

choices.consequence: You jam the tank into the jaws as they come and get your hand back, mostly, and then you climb the mast with the rifle on a strap. You choose to throw it in. By Mast Top, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You fire at the tank while it is still on your own deck. The round goes wide and takes out the compressor instead, and the boat lists further.

nodes.text: You are up in the crosstrees with the mast leaning further every second and the sea climbing to meet your boots. It circles once and turns in, jaw open, the yellow tank wedged back behind the teeth where the throat should be. You brace the rifle across the spreader. Salt in both eyes. Four rounds left. It is close enough now to see what its eye is doing.

choices.consequence: You breathe out, hold, and put the last round into the tank at ten yards, and the whole sea stands straight up in front of you. You aim true. The way toward Smile You opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

You fire early and fast, three rounds wasted into open water, and the fourth is now the one that has to work. You commit to pull the trigger now. It carries you into Quint's Wake while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

There is a version where the fish never comes back for the third pass, and the town has to answer for itself on dry land instead. You commit to take the third path. It carries you into The Mayor Resigns while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The tank goes and the sea stands up white and comes down again in pieces, and the pieces are red. You are hanging off a mast in ten feet of water with your ears ringing and no boat under you. Then Hooper surfaces forty yards out, glasses gone, entirely alive, swearing. You paddle in on a seat cushion and a length of spar, kicking the whole way, and you do not once put your face in the water.

You mark the position on the chart and read something over it that you half remember from a funeral in Queens. Hooper says the man's first name and you find that you never knew it. Afterward, at town meetings and cookouts and school fetes, for thirty years, people ask what Quint was like out there, and you say he knew his business, and change the subject, because the true sentence has no polite version.

Vaughn resigns in October in a letter that mentions his health. The beaches stay shut through Labor Day, two guest houses fold, the ferry runs half empty, and nobody in Amity quite forgives you for having been right. In spring the harbourmaster bolts a sign at the head of the dock that says READ THE WATER. Tourists photograph it, thinking it quaint. You pass it every morning and go nowhere near the end of the pier.
